name: Harvest Table
education: An optional discovery objective about cultivation and food processing. Bread-making predates farming; this gameplay chain is not a universal chronology. Historical explanations are free and reading is not required for the reward.

name: Bronze Workshop
education: Connect earlier gameplay foundations with ore reduction, alloying and working metal. These are discovery objectives, not a complete historical manufacturing procedure.

name: Marks and Materials
education: Explore earlier plant and clay materials alongside writing and records. Writing has independent traditions; this collection does not require one historical sequence or any reading to earn its discovery reward.

name: Mediterranean Inquiry
education: Compare physical finds, ancient reports, and modern interpretations. The regional examples are not one timeline, and reading historical notes is never required for the reward.

name: Classical Civic Life
education: Optional civic discoveries, not a transition from Greek government to Rome or a universal model of democracy. Agora remains a core landmark; these additions do not change age completion. Reading is free and never required for the reward.

name: Classical Engineering
education: An optional engineering objective connecting earlier masonry and water management to structural discoveries. Aqueduct and Arch have pre-Roman precedents; their recipes are associations, not construction instructions. Earlier discoveries retain their original ages.

name: Classical Commerce
education: An optional collection about containers, payment and transport. Coinage and maritime exchange have distinct regional histories and do not begin universally in this chapter.

name: Classical Scholarship
education: Library is an optional scholarly target, not a new required landmark. Earlier text formats and diverse mathematical and philosophical traditions do not form one worldwide timeline. Birds and ancient inquiry are distinct from modern evolutionary explanations.
